question: The landing on a coast from the sea: CNavalInvasionOrder whole, a carried land unit's landing march, the invasion's progress and its two scales, the battle at a landing, its outcome, and the INVADEDUS message.

addresses.name: CNavalInvasionOrder::MayBeGiven
addresses.comment: Slot 11 of the invasion order (type 0x3A5): **may a fleet be told to land its passengers in this province**. In order: the order's unit is a fleet (slot 16); it is in no battle (CUnit +0x11C); the order's province (COrder +0xC) is **land** (template +0x22); slot 8 (CNavalOrder::IsInRange) says it is in range of the fleet's base; the fleet carries at least one unit (CNavy +0x2EC); and **the first passenger's slot 34 (CArmy::MayStandIn) allows the province** - so own, a friend's, nobody's, or a province whose owner or controller the passenger's country is at war with, by CCountry::MayEnterProvince. No port, no coast test beyond what Start finds, no war test. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Read whole off the listing 0x5A0790..0x5A0806 (bare ret, three int3 then Start at 0x5A0810, which the vftable holds at slot 13). The slot numbers are the vftable offsets 0x40, 0x20, 0x2C, 0x88 read off the calls. Wrong if 0x5A07F7's `[edx+0x88]` were not slot 34 of the passenger's table - CArmy slot 34 is 0x5CE2A0, recorded as CArmy::MayStandIn.

addresses.name: CNavalInvasionOrder::Start
addresses.comment: Slot 13: **chooses the sea province the landing is made from** and keeps it at +0x48 (saved as `transport`). Over the target province's edges in their order (template +0x90, 0x14 a step, every kind - impassable edges are not skipped here): a neighbour that is sea (+0x22 clear), simulated (+0x13D) and that the fleet's slot 35 (CanMoveTo) allows is taken where nothing is chosen yet **or** where CMapProvince::NavalDistanceTo(target, neighbour) is strictly less than the distance of the one chosen. **A distance of nought counts as nothing chosen** (the test is `best == 0`), so a candidate at distance 0 - the sea province the target names, or every candidate where the target names none - is replaced by the next one in edge order. Nothing found leaves +0x48 null. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5A0810..0x5A098E: `test ebx, ebx; je` at 0x5A093B on the running best ([ebp-0x14]) before the `cmp ebx,[eax]; jle` at 0x5A0952; NavalDistanceTo (0x4A5570) is called with ecx = [edi+0xC], the order's province, both times. Wrong if [edi+0xC] were not the target - MayBeGiven tests the same field for land.

addresses.name: CNavalInvasionOrder::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14, asked every hour: **the invasion mission**. Fleet with no base (+0x98): false. In a battle: true and nothing else. CNavalOrder::IsActive false: false. COrder +0x18 return_to_base set: true. Has a path: true. **Not at the landing sea (+0x48)**: carrying something -> NavalOrder_GoTo(the landing sea) where one was chosen, true; carrying nothing -> OrderReturnToBase, false. **At the landing sea and carrying**: (1) flanks = every province on the target's edges, edge kind not 3, that is land, whose owner area's slot 0 says yes, whose controller is an enemy of the fleet's owner (CCountry::IsEnemy 0x42F210), that has an edge to the landing sea and holds no enemy land unit (CountEnemyLandUnitsInList); (2) heading = how many passengers' first path province is the target; (3) for each passenger in list order not in a battle: one that cannot fight (slot 33) is kept aside if it has no path; one that can fight but whose slot 35 refuses the target **ends the order** (OrderReturnToBase, false); one with a path is skipped; otherwise e = enemy land units in the target, and where there are flanks and heading < e + 6 and heading < 2e it is sent (NavalOrder_GoTo) to the next flank in turn, otherwise to the target, heading += its brigade count (CUnit +0x40). (4) each passenger kept aside goes to the target, or else to the first flank, for which CUnit::OtherFighterBoundFor says a fighting unit of its country is bound; any left over **end the order** (OrderReturnToBase, false). True. **At the landing sea and empty**: no war with the target's controller -> OrderReturnToBase, false; a land battle in the target (HasCombatOfKind 1) -> true; a retreating unit in the target whose path ends at the fleet's province -> true; otherwise OrderReturnToBase and **true**, the order living on in port. It never asks the too-worn test 0x59A990. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Read whole off the listing 0x5A0990..0x5A102F (bare ret at 0x5A0E9F, 0x5A0F2E, 0x5A0F81, 0x5A1004, 0x5A102F; Ghidra's body agrees). The thresholds are `lea edx,[eax+6]; cmp [esp+0x14],edx; jge` and `add eax,eax; cmp [esp+0x14],eax; jge` at 0x5A0DCE..0x5A0DDD, both jumping to the call that sends the unit to [edx+0xC], the target; the +0x40 add at 0x5A0E04. Wrong if [esp+0x14] were not the heading count - it is written at 0x5A0C7C from the loop at 0x5A0C50 that compares each passenger's first path province with the target.

addresses.name: CNavalInvasionOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of the CPersistent table: CNavalOrder::SaveContents, then `transport` = the landing sea province's id (+0x48, its +0xD0) where one is set. Nothing is written under `message`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5A1160..0x5A11C9 (`ret 4`); held at slot 2 of CNavalInvasionOrder_vftable 0x15C7274 and introduced there per the RTTI export.

addresses.name: CNavalInvasionOrder::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavalInvasionOrder::LoadKey(CNavalInvasionOrder* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 2 of them, one case each: `message`, `transport`. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence. **`transport` (0x3A8) is the landing sea province**: its id read with sscanf and the province stored at +0x48. **`message` (0xE1) is parsed with ParseBool into a byte of the caller's own argument slot ([ebp+0xB]) and thrown away** - the order has no field for it and SaveContents never writes it. Everything else goes to CNavalOrder::LoadKey. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5A1030..: `cmp eax,0x3A8` then the store `mov [edi+0x48],eax` at 0x5A10F9; `cmp eax,0xE1` at 0x5A110F then `lea ecx,[ebp+0xB]; push ecx; call 0xA7B410`. The object is 0x4C bytes (CreateOrder's `push 0x4C` at 0x583B9E), so +0x48 is its last field.
addresses.revises: Adds what each of the two keys does: `transport` is +0x48, `message` is parsed and discarded.

addresses.name: CUnit::MovementProgressShare
addresses.comment: **How far a unit is along the step it is taking, in thousandths**: 0 with no path, -1 where CUnit::MovementDistance is 0, otherwise movement_progress (+0x14C) * 1000 / MovementDistance, truncated (a 64-bit division where the product would overflow). For a unit landing from the sea that is the **invasion's progress** - progress over AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_MOVEMENT_COST - which CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers interpolates the two landing scales by, the battle tooltip prints as AMPH_INVASION_PROGRESS and the battle entry's `combat_unit_bg` bar shows. CUnit::RetreatFromCombat takes the largest of it over the defender's units. The sibling of CUnit::SetMovementProgressShare. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5CA340..0x5CA3CF, `ret 4` on every path, the unit in EAX (`mov esi, eax`), MovementDistance called with ESI. Callers 0x565A9E, 0x565AB4 (RetreatFromCombat), 0x569C95 (slot 19), 0x5D015A, 0x729CC3, 0x72A99B, 0x8BECCF, each loading the unit into EAX first.

addresses.name: CNavy::MeanLandingProgress
addresses.comment: The mean CUnit::MovementProgressShare over the fleet's passengers (CNavy +0x2E4) that are landing on ground an enemy of their owner controls - a land unit with a path, in a sea province, next province land, its controller an enemy (the test of CUnit::IsLandingFromSea, inlined). sum * 1000 / (count * 1000); 0 where there are none. Two callers, 0x5CB790 and 0x5CC1AB, both on the fleet's display side (a float at +0x15C of an object at the fleet's +0x190, the value over 1000). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and checked on the listing: `mov edi,[eax+0x2E4]` at 0x5D00AC, `ret 4` at 0x5D01A3, CCountry::IsEnemy and 0x5CA340 in the loop. What 0x5CB630 does with it was not read past the store at 0x5CB7AE.

addresses.name: CNavy::HasLandingPassenger
addresses.comment: Whether any passenger of the fleet (CNavy +0x2E4) is landing on ground an enemy of its owner controls - CUnit::IsLandingFromSea(unit, false) inlined over the list. Asked by 0x5CB630, the fleet-side display that MeanLandingProgress feeds. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; bare `ret` at 0x5D008D and 0x5D0093, the fleet in EAX (`in_EAX->+0x2E4`), no stack argument read.

addresses.name: CUnit::OtherFighterBoundFor
addresses.comment: Whether **another** land unit of the unit's country (CCountry +0xBAC, its list of units) has a path, can fight (slot 33) and has the province as the **last** province of its path (CUnit +0x13C). Asked by CUnit::AdvanceMovement of a land unit landing on enemy ground that cannot fight itself - yes, it waits the hour; no, its move is cancelled - and by CNavalInvasionOrder::IsActive for the passengers that cannot fight. The other unit need not be landing at all. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5C2F20..0x5C2FD2, `ret 8` on both paths; slot 15 (0x3C), the path count +0x140, slot 33 (0x84), `cmp esi, ebx` for the self test, and the last node +0x13C compared by province id (+0xD0).

addresses.name: InvasionWarnings_IsInvadingPlayer
addresses.comment: Whether a unit is an enemy of the player landing on the player's coast: the player's country (CCurrentGameState +0xC30) is an enemy of the unit's owner (CCountry::IsEnemyTag 0x42F1B0), CUnit::IsLandingFromSea(unit, false), and the first province of its path is **controlled** by the player (+0x338 against +0xC34). The test both sides of the INVADEDUS message use. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x44DBB0..0x44DCBF, bare `ret`; the unit is read through EDI only (`lea eax,[edi+0x124]`, `mov eax, edi` before 0x5C2E80), and both callers set EDI to the unit (0x44DCDE, 0x44DF8F).

addresses.name: InvasionWarnings_Add
addresses.comment: Called by SetUnitPath (0x5C9DAE) on the game state's list of invasion warnings (CCurrentGameState +0x8) for every unit given a path. Where InvasionWarnings_IsInvadingPlayer says yes and the path's first province exists: the entry for the unit's owner (a std::map keyed by country id) is made if missing and its byte `new` (+0x10 of the value) set to whether it was missing; then, where the unit is not yet in the entry's vector of 0x28-byte unit references, it is appended and `new` set. **So re-pathing a unit already listed clears `new`** for its country. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x44DCC0..0x44DE15, `ret 8`: `cmp [eax],esi; sete bl` (find == end) and `mov [eax+0x10],bl` at 0x44DD37..0x44DD4B, the search over 0x28-byte entries at 0x44DD73, the append 0x44F910 and `mov byte [eax+0x10],1` at 0x44DE01. The one caller pushes `[0x1A89790] + 8`.

addresses.name: InvasionWarnings_Hourly
addresses.comment: **Raises INVADEDUS**, the first thing RunHourlyPass does (0x682654, on CCurrentGameState +0x8). Where the player (+0xC30/+0xC34) is not the one the list was kept for (+0x18/+0x1C), the list is emptied and the player taken. Then for each country entry: every listed unit that no longer resolves or no longer passes InvasionWarnings_IsInvadingPlayer is dropped (the scan starting again after each drop); where units are left and the entry's `new` byte is set, it is cleared and **one message** goes to the player: type INVADEDUS, the player's own BuildMessageVariables plus ENEMY = CountryNameOfCountry(the invading country) and PROV = FormatProvinceList(the distinct first path provinces of the listed units, in list order - 'A, B and C'), the message's province the first of them; posted through PostMessage_CInGameIdler. An emptied entry stays in the map. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and checked on the listing 0x44DE20..0x44E610 (bare `ret`, the list in ECX copied to ESI at 0x44DE48): the player compare at 0x44DEC4, `push 9; push 'INVADEDUS'` at 0x44E3F5, the 'ENEMY' and 'PROV' variables, CMessage::CMessage at 0x44E4E6 with the first province pushed at 0x44E4D4, the flag test `(char)local_18[8]` = node +0x20. One caller, 0x682654.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::AddAssaultModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLandCombatant::AddAssaultModifiers(CLandCombatant* this, CUnit* unit, int unknown)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 27, land only, and called for the attacker only** (from 0x16A347, inside `if (is_attacker)`). Decides four modifiers. First it classifies the assault: if the unit's own province is water then amphibious, unless the owner tag is literally 'REB'; otherwise it finds the ProvinceEdge from the unit's province to the combat's province and reads its `kind` - **2 is a river crossing, 1 is a sea crossing** (a strait: amphibious too, with no landing progress).

BM_RIVER_PENALTY (0x0E) at 0x169864: `v = RIVER_CROSSING_PENALTY + unit->+0xC8->river.attack(+0x9C) + GetTraitEffect(unit, 7 river_attack)`; added only when negative, and sets +0x16.

BM_PARATROOP_PENALTY (0x0D) at 0x1698A5: when unit->+0x97 is set, `v = PARADROP_PENALTY + GetTraitEffect(unit, 27 paradrop_mission)`, negative only, sets +0x15, and clears the amphibious flag whatever v is.

BM_AMPH_PENALTY (0x0B) at 0x169A63: `v = AMPHIBIOUS_LANDING_PENALTY + unit->+0xC8->amphibious.attack(+0xB4) + GetTraitEffect(unit, 25 amph_attack)`. **When v is negative, CUnit::IsLandingFromSea(unit, false) and the unit is carried by a fleet** (its slot 9 object's +0x300, CArmy::carried_by - not a naval base of the province, as this said before), the penalty is cut by the fleet: `s = 1000 + sum over the landing unit's regiments of fleet->+0xC8->extra_amphibious_defence map (+0x218, keyed by the regiment definition's type_index +0x24)`, `r = min(s * fleet->+0xC8->amphibious_invasion_defence(+0x18C) / 1000, AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_LANDING_PENALTY_DECREASE)` (-1 where the define is 0), `v = v * (1010 - r * 1000 / cap) / 1000`. **The map on a fleet's summed definition is always empty** - CUnit::RebuildDefinition builds it by Assign of the null definition and Add of each ship, neither of which touches +0x200..+0x223 - so s is 1000 and `extra_amphibious_defence` never reaches this. Then `v = max(v, -990)`. 1010 and -990 are inline floorf of the literals 1010.5 (0x120A7C8) and -989.5 (0x120A7C4), not defines. Sets +0x13.

BM_FORT_MODIFIER (0x0C) at 0x169B3D: `level = prov->modifiers(+0x114)[amphibious ? 11 COASTAL_FORT_LEVEL : 10 FORT_LEVEL] / 1000 * 1000` (truncated to whole levels); for the attacker `v = level * BASE_FORT_PENALTY / 1000 + GetTraitEffect(unit, 8 fort_attack) + unit->+0xC8->fort.attack(+0x84)`, zeroed if positive; **for the defender v is GetTraitEffect(unit, 24 fort_defence) and nothing else** - the fort itself reaches land combat only as the attacker's penalty. Sets +0x14. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md). **The defender's arm of BM_FORT_MODIFIER is never reached**: the one call the record has, at 0x16A347, is behind the side's attacker flag (`cmp byte [ebx+0x38],0; je` at 0x16A335), so a leader's fort_defence trait does nothing in a land battle; other calls of slot 27 were not searched for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-battleleaders.md, section 6, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Re-read whole off the listing 0x569750..0x569B48 (`ret 8`). The carrier: `mov edx,[eax+0x24]; call edx; mov eax,[eax+0x300]` at 0x5698FF..0x569908 is the unit's slot 9 (ReturnThis for a CArmy) and CArmy +0x300, the same pair CUnit::MovementSpeed reads at 0x5C91AB..0x5C91B4 for the fleet's amphibious_invasion_speed. The map: Assign 0x5A7500..0x5A78A8 and Add 0x5A7FC0..0x5A83AA hold no access to +0x200..+0x223, while the copy constructor 0x536570 does copy that sub-object (0x536A24..0x536A6E) - the positive control for the shape a copy would have. Wrong if a CUnit's own +0xC8 were made by the copy constructor; CUnit::CUnit makes it with the named constructor 0x5A3510 (0x5B5396), which builds an empty CSubUnitAmphibiousMult (0x482610 at 0x5A3818).
addresses.revises: Raised to confirmed; BM_AMPH_PENALTY's `+0x300` is the carrying fleet (CArmy::carried_by), not the province's naval base, `+0x218` is the fleet definition's extra_amphibious_defence map (always empty, so s = 1000) and `+0x18C` the fleet's summed amphibious_invasion_defence; the paratroop arm clears the flag whatever its figure.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CLandCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment: **Slot 19 for a land fight**, and the readable example of the family. Calls the base at 0x165590 first (which resets every unit's four multipliers to 1000). Then **the landing scales**, over `units` (+0x40): for a land unit with a path, standing in a sea province, whose next province is land and controlled by an enemy of its owner, `p = CUnit::MovementProgressShare(unit)` and `attack = ATTACK_LOW + (ATTACK_HIGH - ATTACK_LOW) * p / 1000` into CUnit +0xF4, `low = DEFEND_LOW + (the carrying fleet's summed amphibious_invasion_defence, CArmy +0x300 -> +0xC8 -> +0x18C, where it is carried)`, `defence = low + (DEFEND_HIGH - low) * p / 1000` into +0xF8 (AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_*; 64-bit products, truncated). Whether the unit is the attacker is not asked. Then shore bombardment, and the per-unit modifiers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x569B85..0x569D2F: the four defines at +0x280/+0x284/+0x288/+0x28C, the tests at 0x569BF2..0x569C88, `call 0x5CA340` at 0x569C95, the fleet's +0x18C at 0x569CBB, the stores `mov [esi+0xF4],eax` at 0x569CFB and `mov [esi+0xF8],eax` at 0x569D29. A scan of [[x+0xAC]+0x280..0x28C] (fieldchain.py --holder 0xAC) finds these four reads and no other; its positive control, +0x278, finds the known read in CUnit::MovementSpeed.
addresses.revises: Spells out the landing arm: the figure is the step's progress share, the defence's low end has the carrying fleet's amphibious_invasion_defence added, and the attacker is not asked.

addresses.name: CUnit::MovementSpeed
addresses.comment: **What an hour adds to a unit's movement progress**, thousandths. Ordinarily the unit definition's `max_speed` (CUnit +0xC8 then +0x108, the minimum over its brigades) times CUnit::MovementSpeedModifier / 1000, then times LAND_SPEED_MODIFIER, NAVAL_SPEED_MODIFIER or AIR_SPEED_MODIFIER / 1000 by the unit's kind. Two special cases come first: a land unit at sea bound for land and carried by a fleet (CArmy +0x300) moves at **AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_SPEED_BASE plus the carrying fleet's summed amphibious_invasion_speed (+0xC8 -> +0x188, the mean over its ships that declare one) and nothing else** - the function returns there, before MovementSpeedModifier and before LAND_SPEED_MODIFIER, so weather, fuel, terrain and the retreat bonus do not touch a landing; and a land unit under a strategic redeployment order (type 0x5A4) at STRAT_REDEP_BASE_SPEED times a clamped figure of the province's infrastructure. Infrastructure is no part of an ordinary march. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5C91AB..0x5C91E4: slot 9, `[eax+0x300]`, `[ecx+0x188]`, the define at +0x278, `add ecx, esi; mov [eax], ecx` and straight to the epilogue.
addresses.revises: Says that the landing speed returns before every modifier and LAND_SPEED_MODIFIER.

structs.name: CNavalInvasionOrder
structs.comment: The fleet's invasion mission, order type 0x3A5 (ORDER_INVADE, 'Land troops, carried on the fleet, in the selected province'). COrder +0xC is the province to land on; its own field is the sea province the landing is made from. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
structs.evidence: CreateOrder allocates 0x4C bytes (`push 0x4C` at 0x583B9E), calls the CNavalOrder constructor 0x59A900, writes vftable 0x15C7274 and zeroes +0x48 (0x583BC5..0x583BCB); RTTI gives CNavalOrder as its only base, at offset 0.

struct_fields.name: landing_sea
struct_fields.comment: The sea province beside the target from which the passengers land, chosen by Start and saved as `transport`. IsActive sails the fleet there and only lands from there; null where Start found none, and then the order does nothing.
struct_fields.evidence: Written by CNavalInvasionOrder::Start at 0x5A0956 and LoadKey at 0x5A10F9 (`transport`), zeroed by CreateOrder at 0x583BCB, saved by SaveContents; compared with the fleet's province (+0x130) at 0x5A0A09.

struct_fields.name: landing_attack_scale
struct_fields.comment: **The landing's attack scale**, thousandths: 1000 but for a land unit landing from the sea on enemy ground, for which CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (slot 19) sets AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_ATTACK_LOW + (HIGH - LOW) * CUnit::MovementProgressShare / 1000 every battle hour after CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers put it back to 1000. CLandCombatant::FireUnit multiplies the unit's shot count by +0xEC * +0xF4 / 1000 (0x16AED2); the battle tooltip prints it as AMPH_INVASION_ATTACK_SCALE where it is not 1000 and folds it into the Attack Modifier.
struct_fields.evidence: Every store at [reg+0xF4] fieldchain.py lists in a CUnit-shaped function: the constructor (0x5B5148), ResetCombatModifiers (0x5C302F) and the landing arm (0x569CFB); the 0x5B7C35 store in CUnit::LoadKey is through the CPersistent pointer at +8, so it lands at +0xFC. Readers: 0x56AED2 (FireUnit), 0x566393 (slot 11), 0x72ABBC (tooltip).
struct_fields.revises: Renamed from combat_attack_modifier_b: the only figure ever written here other than 1000 is the landing's attack scale.

struct_fields.name: landing_defend_scale
struct_fields.comment: **The landing's defence scale**, thousandths: 1000 but for a land unit landing from the sea on enemy ground, for which slot 19 sets low + (AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_DEFEND_HIGH - low) * MovementProgressShare / 1000 with low = AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_DEFEND_LOW + the carrying fleet's summed amphibious_invasion_defence. CLandCombatant::FireUnit multiplies the unit's defence as a target by +0xF0 * +0xF8 / 1000 (0x16B0CB); the tooltip prints it as AMPH_INVASION_DEFEND_SCALE where it is not 1000.
struct_fields.evidence: Stores at 0x569D29 (landing arm) and 0x5C3035 (reset) and the constructor; reader 0x56B0CB in FireUnit, 0x566376 in slot 11, 0x72ACEC in the tooltip.
struct_fields.revises: Renamed from combat_defend_modifier_b, for the same reason.

struct_fields.name: amphibious_invasion_defence
struct_fields.comment: the `amphibious_invasion_defence` key. **A plain sum**, unlike its `_speed` neighbour, so it scales with the number of brigades - or ships: it is read **off the carrying fleet's summed definition** (the landing unit's CArmy +0x300, then +0xC8), at 0x16991F in BM_AMPH_PENALTY and at 0x169CBB where slot 19 adds it to AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_DEFEND_LOW. The technology amphibious_assault_units raises it on transport_ship, invasion_transport_ship and assault_ship.
struct_fields.evidence: Both reads go through `call [vft+0x24]; mov eax,[eax+0x300]; mov eax,[eax+0xC8]` (0x5698FF..0x569916, 0x569CA0..0x569CB5): slot 9 of the landing unit, then CArmy::carried_by, then the fleet's own definition.
struct_fields.revises: The reads are of the carrying fleet's definition, not the landing unit's own.

struct_fields.name: amphibious_invasion_speed
struct_fields.comment: the `amphibious_invasion_speed` key. Summed by `Add`, but `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` then **overwrites it with the mean over the brigades that declare a non-zero one** (0x1B6183..0x1B61D6). **CUnit::MovementSpeed** reads it at 0x1C91C4 off the carrying fleet's definition (CArmy +0x300 -> +0xC8) and adds AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_SPEED_BASE (`CDefines + 0xAC` then +0x278) to it, so a mean over the fleet's ships is the right shape there. The technology amphibious_invasion_technology raises it on the three transport types.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x5C91C4 lies in CUnit::MovementSpeed (0x5C9140); functionStart misattributes it to 0x5C8D10. The fleet: `mov eax,[eax+0x300]; mov ecx,[eax+0xC8]` at 0x5C91B4..0x5C91BE.
struct_fields.revises: The reader is CUnit::MovementSpeed, not MovementSpeedModifier, and the definition is the carrying fleet's.

struct_fields.name: extra_amphibious_defence
struct_fields.comment: The `extra_amphibious_defence` key (save token 0x83B). **The vftable of an embedded CSubUnitAmphibiousMult** (0x15BDD5C), a CPersistent of 0x24 bytes running to +0x223: its LoadKey takes each key as a unit type's name and its value; at +0x218 a std::map keyed by a sub unit type_index (head +0x21C, size +0x220). BM_AMPH_PENALTY looks the landing unit's regiments up in the **carrying fleet's** summed definition's map - and that one is always empty, since CUnit::RebuildDefinition's Assign and Add never copy this sub-object. Only the copy constructor 0x536570 does.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x482610 writes vftable 0x15BDD5C at +0 and makes the map's head at +0x1C (= +0x21C) with size 0 at +0x20; CSubUnitDefinition's named constructor calls it on +0x200 (0x5A3818); RTTI names the vftable's class CSubUnitAmphibiousMult. Assign (0x5A7500) and Add (0x5A7FC0) hold no access between +0x200 and +0x223.
struct_fields.revises: Says what lies there: an embedded CSubUnitAmphibiousMult with its map at +0x218, and that a unit's summed definition never carries one.

struct_fields.name: extra_amphibious_defence_head
struct_fields.comment: The head node of the extra_amphibious_defence map (the map object at +0x218, size at +0x220) - the end() BM_AMPH_PENALTY compares a lookup with (0x169939, 0x169965). Its nodes hold the key at +0xC and the value, thousandths, at +0x10.

struct_fields.name: invasion_warnings_player
struct_fields.comment: **The tag of the player the list of invasion warnings (+0x8) was kept for**, with its id at +0x1C. InvasionWarnings_Hourly compares the id with the player's (+0xC34) every hour and, where they differ, empties the list and copies +0xC30/+0xC34 here. That settles both readings this field had: the null tag `---` before the first hour of a session, the player's own tag (`IRE`) after it.

struct_fields.revises: Named: it is the invasion warnings' copy of the player's tag, which explains both earlier readings.

struct_fields.name: invasion_warnings_player_id

struct_fields.name: invasion_warnings_head
struct_fields.comment: **The list of invasion warnings** is a std::map from +0x8 (head here, count at +0x10): one entry per country whose units are landing on the player's coast, keyed by country id, its value a vector of 0x28-byte unit references and a byte `new` at +0x10. Filled by InvasionWarnings_Add from SetUnitPath, read and pruned by InvasionWarnings_Hourly, which raises INVADEDUS from it.
